en: If you hear thunder within 30 seconds of seeing lightning, you are close enough to be struck and must seek indoor shelter.
When the heat index exceeds 40 degrees Celsius, your body cannot cool itself through sweating, making heatstroke a serious risk.
Washing root vegetables like carrots removes soil particles that might contain harmful bacteria or parasite eggs before you eat them.
Sunscreens containing the mineral zinc oxide physically block harmful ultraviolet rays from damaging your skin cells.
Boiling floodwater for one minute kills waterborne pathogens like cholera bacteria, making it safer to drink during typhoon emergencies.
Exposing your arms to direct sunlight for 15 minutes helps your body produce Vitamin D, which strengthens your bones.
Finding the North Star, Polaris, helps you determine true north at night if you get lost in a wilderness area.
During a full moon, stronger gravitational pulls create higher spring tides that can cause unexpected, dangerous rip currents for swimmers.
If you feel strong shaking near the coast, immediately evacuate to higher ground because a tsunami might follow the earthquake.
Wearing an N95 mask during volcanic ashfall prevents fine silica particles from entering your lungs and causing breathing problems.
Avoiding wading in floodwaters prevents leptospirosis, a severe bacterial infection spread through the urine of infected rats.
Securing loose roof sheets before a typhoon prevents them from becoming dangerous flying projectiles in high-speed winds.
